MOLECULAR CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT

Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Progressive cognitive decline, seizures, right frontal lobe mass
Clinical Diagnosis: Diffuse glioma
Family History: None reported

TEST PERFORMED
Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Analysis
- 1p36 deletion probe (Vysis LSI 1p36/LSI 1q25 Dual Color Probe)
- 19q13 deletion probe (Vysis LSI 19q13/19p13 Dual Color Probe)

SPECIMEN TYPE
Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue from right frontal lobe mass

METHODOLOGY
FISH analysis was performed on 5-micron tissue sections following standard protocols. Hybridization was carried out using commercially available probes for detection of 1p36 and 19q13 deletions. A minimum of 200 non-overlapping tumor nuclei were scored by two independent observers.

RESULTS

Chromosome 1p36 Status: DELETED
Chromosome 19q13 Status: DELETED

Quantitative Analysis:
- Total nuclei analyzed: 200
- Nuclei with 1p36/19q13 codeletion: 184
- Percentage of cells with codeletion: 92%

Detailed Scoring:
- 1p36 deletion: 184/200 nuclei (92%)
- 19q13 deletion: 184/200 nuclei (92%)
- Concurrent 1p36/19q13 codeletion: 184/200 nuclei (92%)

INTERPRETATION
This FISH analysis demonstrates 1p/19q codeletion in 92% of analyzed tumor nuclei, which is well above the diagnostic threshold of 30%. The presence of 1p/19q codeletion is a defining molecular feature of oligodendroglioma according to the WHO CNS tumor classification.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
1. Diagnostic: The 1p/19q codeletion confirms the diagnosis of oligodendroglioma (WHO CNS classification)
2. Prognostic: This molecular alteration is associated with:
   - Favorable overall prognosis
   - Longer progression-free survival
   - Better overall survival compared to gliomas without codeletion
3. Predictive: Enhanced sensitivity to chemotherapy, particularly alkylating agents

RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on the molecular findings and current evidence-based guidelines:
1. Consider combined alkylating agent therapy with nitrosourea plus radiation, given the enhanced chemosensitivity of 1p/19q codeleted tumors
2. The favorable molecular profile supports aggressive treatment approaches
3. Clinical correlation with histopathologic findings and IDH mutation status is recommended for complete molecular characterization

REPORTED BY
[redacted name], Ph.D., FACMG
Director, Molecular Cytogenetics Laboratory
